title: QuADMESH: A Quadrangular ADvanced, automatic unstructured MESH generator for 2D shallow-water models
description:
QuADMESH is a Python port of the QuADMESH+ method for converting two-dimensional triangular meshes of hydrodynamic domains into quadrilaterals, published by Mattioli in a 2017 thesis. It merges adjacent triangle pairs one element layer at a time, from the innermost layer outward toward the boundary. The conversion reuses the input vertices, leaves no interior residual triangle, and returns a quad-pure mesh by default. A post-processing routine can clear triangles left over on the boundary. Mesh layers, smoothing and quality metrics come from CHILmesh. The entry point is tri2quad, with a command-line interface in quadmesh.cli. Install with pip install quadmesh; the import name is quadmesh.

This release (0.2.6)

Fixed

  • The per-layer sweep is conforming again. Leftover triangles fell through to edge_insertion, whose split is blocked by the #81 guard, so each insertion left a hanging node. The sweep now closes each leftover triangle on its live outer ring by a ring-edge split or a vertex split and never collapses an edge. preserve_boundary=True still loses no boundary vertex.

Changed

  • The bundled thesis PDF is a rebuild from the LaTeX source with every cross-reference and citation resolved; the OhioLINK copy prints ?? and [?]. The corrected PDF is archived at 10.5281/zenodo.23607233 and attached to each GitHub release.
  • Contact lines use GitHub profile links in place of email addresses.

Removed

  • quadmesh._topology, a private wrapper module with no callers; code calls the CHILmesh topology APIs directly.

Known limitation: some boundary-layer quads can be concave.

Roadmap at 0.2.6

  • Now: boundary-layer quality, including the ENPAC2003 low-skew tail (#90); right-size the test suite (#109).
  • Next: boundary-type-aware layer seeding (#77); a MATLAB parity oracle (#116); wire tri2quad(aggressive=) to CHILmesh merge_elements.
  • Later: parallelization (#38); evaluate a C++ or Rust backend; formal integration with ADMESH and CHILmesh.
